planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Miss Christine was named by breeder Sheila Chapman for her daughter.

directions: Plant with roots shaded and cool while the vine climbs into full sun to light shade on a sturdy support. Miss Christine bears single white flowers edged in pale pink with cream-flushed buds, sweetly fragrant and opening in a single flush from late spring into early summer. It was named by its breeder, Sheila Chapman, for her daughter, and shares the vigorous climbing habit typical of Clematis montana selections. It flowers on the previous year's growth, so prune only right after bloom.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Margaret Jones is a vigorous climber blooming in a single spring flush on old wood.

directions: Plant with roots shaded and cool while the vine climbs into full sun to light shade on a sturdy support. Margaret Jones is a vigorous deciduous climber bearing pale pink single to semi-double flowers in a single spring flush on the previous year's growth, typical of the montana group's vigor and reliability. Give it ample room, since montana clematis can quickly cover a large pergola, fence, or outbuilding. Prune only right after flowering to control size without removing next year's buds.

common_name: Olga Clematis Montana (Deep Pink, Bronze Foliage)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Olga arose as a seedling found by its namesake, Olga Cadge.

directions: Plant with roots shaded and cool while the vine climbs into full sun to light shade on a sturdy support. Olga bears flowers in a deeper pink than the typical var. rubens forms, with bronze-red young foliage and red stems adding color before and after the fairly fragrant late-spring bloom. It arose as a seedling found by Olga Cadge and shares the vigorous climbing habit and pruning needs of other montana selections, blooming on the previous year's growth.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Prosperity sometimes repeats bloom in late summer or autumn, unusual for this group.

directions: Plant with roots shaded and cool while the vine climbs into full sun to light shade on a sturdy support. Prosperity produces a mass of long-stemmed, bright white flowers in a strong mid-season flush, with some repeat bloom in late summer or autumn, an unusual bonus for a montana-group clematis that typically flowers only once. Reaching 20 feet or more, it needs a large, sturdy support to show off its full vigor. Prune lightly right after the main spring flush to avoid removing the chance of autumn repeat bloom.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Jacqui shows an unusual mix of flower forms on the same plant.

directions: Plant with roots shaded and cool while the vine climbs into full sun to light shade on a sturdy support. Jacqui produces a distinctive mixture of double, semi-double, and single flowers on the same plant, white with a pink-tinged reverse and creamy-yellow stamens, sweetly scented and blooming from May into June. This variability in flower form from bloom to bloom is an unusual and collectible trait within the montana group. Prune lightly right after flowering, since it blooms on the previous year's wood.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Pleniflora is historically the first double-flowered Clematis montana selection.

directions: Plant with roots shaded and cool while the vine climbs into full sun to light shade on a very sturdy, large support. Pleniflora bears lacy, semi-double white flowers that face upward rather than outward, an unusual orientation within the montana group, historically documented as the first double-flowered Clematis montana selection introduced. It is extremely vigorous, reaching 25 feet or more, but is reported to be slightly less cold-hardy than typical montana cultivars. Prune lightly right after flowering to manage its substantial size.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Sunrise was raised by Robin and Laura Mitchell in New Zealand and registered in 1996.

directions: Plant with roots shaded and cool while the vine climbs into full sun to light shade on a sturdy support. Sunrise, raised by Robin and Laura Mitchell in New Zealand in 1991 and registered in 1996, bears double or semi-double pink flowers clustered densely at each node, giving a fuller appearance than single-flowered montana cultivars. It blooms on the previous year's growth in a single spring flush typical of the group. Prune lightly right after flowering to maintain shape without sacrificing next year's bloom.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Stolwijk Gold is a patented selection grown as much for its chartreuse foliage as its flowers.

directions: Plant with roots shaded and cool while the vine climbs into full sun to light shade on a modest trellis. Stolwijk Gold stands out among alpina selections for its bright golden-green to chartreuse foliage, paired with single, nodding, lavender-blue bell flowers with white centers in spring. Reaching 8-13 feet, it is a patented selection that functions equally as a foliage accent and a flowering vine. Prune only lightly right after flowering, since it blooms on the previous year's growth.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Frankie is compact enough for a north- or east-facing wall or a container.

directions: Plant with roots shaded and cool while the vine climbs into full sun to light shade, performing especially well on a cooler north- or east-facing wall. Frankie is a Royal Horticultural Society award-winning alpina selection bearing broad, bell-shaped, light-to-mid blue flowers in early spring, followed by fluffy, decorative seed heads. Its compact size, about 6.5 feet tall and 5 feet wide, suits a smaller garden or large container better than the more vigorous montana-group clematis. Prune lightly right after flowering to maintain its tidy shape.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Burford White is one of the hardier alpina selections, surviving to roughly zone 3b.

directions: Plant with roots shaded and cool while the vine climbs into full sun to light shade on a modest trellis. Burford White bears creamy white, four-petaled, nodding bell flowers, sometimes with the stems and flowers clustered unusually close together, over light green foliage. Reaching 6.5-10 feet, it is one of the hardier alpina selections, tolerating winters down to roughly zone 3b, colder than many other clematis in this group. Prune only lightly right after flowering, since it blooms on the previous year's growth.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Foxy is listed within the Atragene group of alpina-type clematis by the International Clematis Society.

directions: Plant with roots shaded and cool while the vine climbs into full sun to light shade on a modest trellis or through a small shrub. Foxy bears pale pink, nodding bell-shaped flowers typical of the alpina form, opening in early spring on the previous year's wood. Its size and habit, 5-8 feet tall and spread, is similar to other alpina cultivars, making it a good companion planting alongside Frances Rivis or other early-spring alpine clematis for a varied color display. Prune only lightly right after flowering.
